description: Internet-wide ingress to an entry point
details: A security group admits 0.0.0.0/0 (or ::/0) to this element, so any internet client can reach it. On its own this is often intended (a public load balancer); it becomes the first hop of an attack path when what sits behind it holds credentials or data.
prerequisites: None: reachable from any internet address.
mitigations: Restrict ingress to known client ranges, place the entry point behind an authenticated edge (WAF, OIDC/Cognito listener), or make it internal.
example: An ALB security group ingress rule with cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] on port 443.

description: Instance role credentials reachable through SSRF (IMDSv1)
details: The instance allows IMDSv1 and has an instance profile. Any server-side request forgery in the workload can fetch the role's temporary credentials from the instance metadata service without a session token.
condition: target.imdsV1Allowed is True and target.hasInstanceRole is True
prerequisites: workload_ssrf: the attacker can make the workload issue HTTP requests (SSRF) or execute code.
mitigations: Require IMDSv2: metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }. Scope the role to what the workload needs.
example: metadata_options { http_tokens = "optional" } on an instance with iam_instance_profile set.

details: Traffic from the internet reaches this workload (directly or through a load balancer) and the workload runs with an IAM role. A compromise of the application becomes a compromise of the role.
condition: target.internetReachable is True and target.hasInstanceRole is True
prerequisites: workload_rce or workload_ssrf: the attacker can make the workload act on their behalf.
mitigations: Keep internet-facing tiers free of data-plane permissions; move data access to a separate, non-exposed service; scope the role.
example: An ALB forwarding to an EC2 instance whose instance profile grants S3 read.

description: Workload identity can read or write classified data
details: The IAM role this workload assumes is allowed to read or write a data store classified confidential or restricted.
prerequisites: The attacker obtains the workload's credentials or controls the workload.
mitigations: Grant only the actions and resources the workload needs; separate roles for workloads that handle classified data.
example: Resource = ["arn:aws:s3:::*"] on a role used by a web tier, with a bucket tagged DataClassification = confidential in the account.

description: Classified data store reachable through a wildcard-resource grant
details: An IAM statement with a wildcard resource (for example arn:aws:s3:::*) covers this classified data store, so access follows from the wildcard rather than from an intentional grant.
condition: target.readableViaWildcardGrant is True and target.storesSensitiveData is True
prerequisites: A principal holding the wildcard grant is compromised.
mitigations: Name the resources in the grant; add an explicit Deny for classified stores to roles that should never touch them.

description: Bucket policy or ACL grants anonymous access
details: A bucket policy or ACL allows any principal. If S3 Block Public Access does not neutralise it, anyone on the internet can use the granted actions.
prerequisites: None when the grant is effective.
mitigations: Remove the public grant, or enable block_public_policy / restrict_public_buckets (and block/ignore public ACLs).
example: Principal = "*" with s3:GetObject in a bucket policy.

details: The function has a URL with authorization_type = NONE, so anyone on the internet can invoke it and act with its role.
mitigations: Use authorization_type = "AWS_IAM", or put the function behind an authenticated API.
